hook.text: Patients preferred a longer, painful procedure over a shorter one if the ending was less painful.

buildup.text: Kahneman found we judge experiences by their peak moment and how they end, not by total duration.

discovery.text: This is the peak-end rule. A great finale rewrites how the whole experience felt in memory.

twist.text: Duration neglect means a 20-minute bad meeting and a 60-minute one feel equally bad if the peak matches.

climax.text: Restaurants serve great desserts for this reason. The ending shapes the whole recalled experience.

punchline.text: End well; they'll remember it well.

quiz.question: What two moments define how we remember an experience?
options: The peak moment and the ending
